_meta.pattern_credit: Profile shape adapted from Bench Studio (MIT, promptadvisers/bench-studio-public), which models per-endpoint prompt knowledge as hot-reloadable JSON rather than prose. The content below is ours.
_meta.verification_note: Every 'measured' field comes from renders.db — 203 ledgered clips of our own, not from vendor marketing. Every 'documented' field comes from our own CLAUDE.md or RUNBOOK and has NOT been independently re-verified against the live API. Anything we have never actually run is in unverified_flags and must not be relied on before a probe.
unverified_flags: resolutions 720p and 1080p: we have only ever submitted 480p (24/24 parameterised rows). Cost and availability at higher resolutions are unknown — do not quote them.

durations below 5 s and above 15 s: our runner clamps to 4-15 but we have only ever submitted 5 s and 10 s. 15 s is attested by exactly one charge (132.17 cr on afterhours/sd_04, which paid and returned no video).
reference images beyond 4: the documented cap is 9 and the runner slices to 9, but the most we have ever actually sent is 4.
t2v mode: the code path exists in run_crun.py and has never been run.
credit-to-USD rate is derived from one project's own reconciliation ($11.18 / 2294.2 cr). It is not a published rate and may not include taxes or top-up fees.

duration_s.evidence: measured — 2 clips at 5 s, 22 at 10 s, all succeeded

max_refs.evidence: documented cap 9 (CLAUDE.md, runner slices refs[:9]); measured max actually submitted is 4

audio.evidence: documented — every clip we ship carries a generated audio track

return_last_frame.evidence: measured — the last frame arrives as an extra entry in result.media_urls[1:], NOT a named field

pricing.evidence: 22 clips at 10 s billed exactly 88.24 cr each (zero variance); 2 clips at 5 s billed exactly 44.30 cr. Both give 8.824 cr/s. One 15 s charge of 132.17 cr agrees (8.81 cr/s).
pricing.unquotable_note: We have never bought a frame above 480p. Refuse to quote rather than guess — a wrong multiplier is worse than no number.

prompt.prompt_style: Twelve named blocks in fixed order, one per line-group, written as plain declarative prose. No markdown, no bullet characters, no 'cinematic' vocabulary. The model reads it as a shot brief, not as a poem: concrete nouns, stated directions, real light.
prompt.structure_template: FORMAT · LOOK · REFERENCE ROLES · CAST · SETTING · STARTING STATE · TIMELINE · CAMERA · CONTINUITY · AUDIO · ENDING STATE · CONSTRAINTS
prompt.length_evidence: measured across the 26 santan v2 shot docs, all of which rendered clean on first QC. min 607, median 646, max 680. This is a house band, not a vendor limit.
do: Give the shot exactly three beats for a 10 s clip (0-3.5 / 3.5-7 / 7-10), three to four for 15 s
Give every @ImageN reference exactly one job AND a do-not-copy clause naming what to ignore in that plate
Name in CAST every body that can appear in frame, and state that every figure, shoulder, hand or reflection at any frame edge belongs to one of them
Write ENDING STATE as a specific description of where people are and how the room looks at the last frame — it is the next clip's continuity reference
Write AUDIO positive-first: state the spoken language, name who is heard, say everyone else keeps their mouth closed, and only then list exclusions
Describe light by direction and quality, and let it be imperfect — clipped highlights, heavy shadows, real grain
dont: Never describe a face, features, skin tone or hair when a reference plate is attached — text describing a face competes with the plate and loses
Never write 'cinematic', or trailer/VFX vocabulary; it pulls the output toward rendered CGI
Never retell the previous clip, and never chain across a location or time cut
Never request multiple shots, cuts, dissolves or scene changes in one generation
Never write nudity, exposed chest or sexual touching — moderation 451 fires on input AND output
Never restate a locked API parameter (duration, aspect ratio, resolution) as prose; set it on the request instead
reference_image_prompt_rules: Describe MOTION and ROLE, never appearance. Restating how a referenced person or object looks gives the model licence to re-invent it.
Address references positionally as @Image1..@ImageN, matching the order they are sent in reference_images.
State the exact number of references attached. With exactly one reference, add: never refer to a second, third or background image; anything not in that one image must be described in words instead.
Give a chained last-frame reference a deliberately narrow job: it controls only the room, its light and where people are standing — do not copy its framing.
A character sheet is the identity anchor: 'the exact person shown in @ImageN, face and hair unchanged, wearing exactly the outfit from that plate'.
Always add the do-not-copy clause for sheet plates: do not copy the white studio background, the split-screen layout, the passport framing or the standing pose.

known_failures.451: Moderation, fires on input AND output. Re-register modestly, keep the beat, add an explicit no-contact negative. Credits charged: 0.
known_failures.422_download_media: Vendor could not fetch a reference URL. Usually a stale upload (uguu deletes after ~3 h), not a vendor fault. Credits charged: 0.
known_failures.422_context_deadline: Transient vendor-side fetch timeout. Retry. Credits charged: 0.
known_failures.truncated_download: File under 400 KB, or over the floor but with no moov atom. Task id is still live, so re-download costs nothing.
known_failures.no_last_frame: Breaks the chain silently. Check media_urls[1:] before trusting the clip.
